OpenMotion

OpenMotion is the first full-stack agentic video generator. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to recreate it with your own brand kit and copy.

  • 🎬 Full-stack video recreation. Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project.
  • 🔑 BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys. OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in your local agent and use your own API keys at every layer.
  • 🧩 OpenMotion introduces Motion.md, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot.
  • 🎛️ Images, video, music and voice. Generate artwork with Nano Banana 2, add a shot with Seedance 2.0, score it with Suno v4 and narrate it with Kokoro. Explore all seven built-in models.

Install from ChatGPT Marketplace

Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/install.md and follow the instructions to install and connect OpenMotion in the current agent.

After setup, the agent opens the local template library and suggests a template. Confirm the choice before creating a project. Source installation guide

Run the repository locally

Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git
cd openmotion
npm ci
npm run build:studio
npm start

✨ Why OpenMotion

1. The first full-stack agentic video generator

Code video with HTML. OpenMotion uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript to describe scenes, typography, layout, transitions and timing. Recorded footage, generated clips, images, music and voice-over become media inside the composition. The same project opens in Studio and renders to MP4.

Write it. Watch it. Change it. Render it. Ask your agent to replace the product, tighten the hook, add a presenter, change the captions or try another ending. It edits the project source; you review the result in the visual editor. Local MCP clients use the project tools, while agents with shell access can follow the Skills and pinned CLI workflow. Agent setup · Native composition guide · Example HTML project

If historical media are unavailable, an Agent restore is refused before changing the project. The editor shows a dismissible error with the affected file paths and confirms that the current project is unchanged.

Review your video, arrange clips and export from the same Studio workspace.

What you can change in Studio

In the Studio What you can do today
Story and timeline Import and arrange media; have the agent trim, reorder and revise against a script or confirmed timecodes
Motion and captions Author animated type, transitions, callouts, charts and captions around your content
Media and sound Import your material and generate images, video, music and TTS voice-over through the built-in model integrations
Image revision Generate candidates with a reference-capable image model and adopt a replacement while preserving timing and animation
Preview and versions Review in Studio, edit by hand or with your agent, and return to the project for the next revision
Export and source Render a fixed version to MP4 and retain the HTML, CSS, JavaScript and media

“Keep the reveal we approved. Replace the middle scene with this screen recording, tighten the opening using these timecodes, and hold our final CTA for two more seconds.”

Projects and versions

From a reference clip to an editable remake

  1. Break down the reference. Pick a sequence. Record its shot order, transitions and sound cues in Motion.md, and mark what you want to replace.
  2. Rebuild the shots. Your agent rebuilds the HTML scenes using your brand kit, copy and visuals, then arranges them on an editable timeline in Studio.
  3. Compare the cuts. Watch the same moment in the original and the remake. Adjust the timing, movement and sound, then play the sequence through.
  4. Export and share. Render the MP4 and keep the HTML source and media. To share a project others can adapt, include its Motion.md, a preview and assets you can redistribute. Project contribution checklist

2. Free and open source. Use your local agent and bring your own keys.

Choose your agent. WorkBuddy, Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness have installation instructions. Other buttons open the shared MCP and CLI setup.

Bring your own… Make it work for your video
🤖 Agent — BYOA Connect your existing local agent through Skills and MCP, with CLI access where supported. Keep your preferred client, account and working context.
🔑 Keys — BYOK Connect supported media-provider API keys in Model Settings. Choose models for images, video, music and TTS; supported local media integrations can use your existing agent login.
🎨 Brand and material Add your logo, fonts, screenshots, camera footage, script and music. Keep identity and approved assets in the Brand Kit section of Motion.md.
🧩 Starting resources Browse references, motion components, templates and community Skills. Pick a direction, give the source or reference to your agent, and make it yours.

The OpenMotion creation pipeline is open source: Skills, project tools, model integrations, Studio and rendering. Run it locally, inspect the implementation and extend the parts you need. OpenMotion charges no software subscription or per-render fee for this local workflow. You can also work with your own footage, images and audio without invoking media-generation APIs.

Provider credentials stay in your workspace, separate from the video project. Your agent and media providers bill any subscriptions or usage to your own accounts. Agent setup and compatibility

3. 100+ Motion.md guides for video recreation

OpenMotion introduces Motion.md: a Markdown format for shot order, timing, transitions and the assets you can replace. The online library brings reference videos and their motion guides into the same detail page.

The Brand Kit section records your identity, voice and approved product facts; the Design section can reference an independent DESIGN.md for visual rules. Keep the reference’s motion and pacing while making the result recognizably yours.

To share an industry or brand system, use the Motion Package v0.2 draft and authoring toolkit. A package combines the design and motion documents with materials, declared dependencies and optional SKILL.md. The included recipe demonstrates two content presets; automatic Studio import and rendered fidelity remain separate from package validation.

Find a template, then make it yours

Browse by reference brand, use case and video type, or search for a specific idea. A template detail page brings together the preview, visual style, production notes and Motion.md download. Choose Recreate template in Studio to copy a prompt for your agent.

Reference-only entries start a reconstruction workflow. When editable source is available, your agent can adapt the project directly.

Browse the template library

4. Multimodal generation: images, video, music and speech

BYOK makes your multimodal accounts part of the video workflow. Add your supported provider keys in Model Settings, choose your models, and generate images, video, music and speech through the Studio's Model Gateway. Preview candidates and adopt the results into the same project your agent and Studio edit. The supported local image path can reuse your existing agent login.

Make what the video needs Built-in model catalog examples Bring it into your film
🖼️ Images Codex Image; Nano Banana 2 via Atlas Cloud; FLUX Schnell via fal.ai Brand visuals, scene artwork and supporting images; reference-based editing through the supported Codex image path
🎬 Video Seedance 2.0 via Atlas Cloud; Wan 2.2 via fal.ai Generated shots and B-roll to combine with your footage and motion
🎵 Music Suno v4 via Atlas Cloud A soundtrack built around your mood and creative brief
🎙️ TTS / voice-over Kokoro via fal.ai Narration from your approved script, placed alongside the visuals and music

“Use the Brand Kit section of our Motion.md and our approved script. Generate artwork for the opening, a video insert, background music and TTS narration. Add the selected results to the recreated project, align the sound and visuals, then show me the full cut.”

Model catalog · Provider setup and endpoints

🛠️ Setup and technical documentation

When choosing or replacing media, creation workflows share a material sourcing policy: reuse suitable supplied assets, prefer original sources for established subjects, and create original/supporting visuals as needed. Explicit user constraints and each workflow’s supported scope still apply.

Install from source

For agent-led installation, use the installation instruction above. To run from source, follow the steps below.

After a successful Agent-led installation, open the editor's template library in the current conversation, without creating a project. Browse and preview first; choose Open and edit to create an independent editable copy. Setup provides a direct library link even before the chat reloads MCP. See the installation reply rules.

During video creation and editing, the chat stays free of preview areas. OpenMotion presents the editable Studio when the final video is ready to preview, then shows the final video in chat after its MP4 export completes and passes verification. Native-host acceptance of an installed build remains separate.

If MCP tools are missing or fail to connect, use the installed connection diagnosis and recovery guide to inspect the actual host configuration and verify the original workspace before continuing.

Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1. Source-based preview and export also need Chrome/Chromium and FFmpeg/FFprobe. Runtime setup

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git
cd openmotion
npm ci
npm run build:studio
npm start

Full reference videos and optional template archives download through Git LFS only when requested. README images/GIFs and built-in templates remain available directly. See clone size and optional media downloads.

Open the studioUrl or previewUrl printed by npm start, then open Template library. Startup reuses a compatible service for the same workspace or selects an available local port. The service keeps running in the background after the launcher exits.

Select a template and choose Recreate template to copy the instruction for your agent. Keep projects and credentials outside the checkout; MOTION_DATA_DIR selects the workspace.

Source checkouts load templates from library/templates/catalog/. The local Studio and MCP use the same files; openmotion_list_templates returns a searchable local index, and openmotion_get_template returns local guide content and absolute source paths. Imported large images and videos retain existing CMS links; new contribution media can use Git LFS. Local edits appear on the next catalog read.

The plugin root is this checkout: .codex-plugin/plugin.json loads its skills/ and .mcp.json, which launches the root mcp.ts. Start stdio with npm run mcp or use an absolute path in manual MCP configuration. Local template workflow.

Bring it into your agent

For Codex with plugin support, run from the checkout:

bash scripts/install-motion.command

WorkBuddy · Import the OpenMotion connector in WorkBuddy or add its mcp.json as a custom MCP server. Ask WorkBuddy to list the available video templates. WorkBuddy setup

Claude Code · Select --host claude in the local installer, then run /mcp in Claude Code to check the connection. Local installation guide

DeepSeek · Work with the editable HTML project from the terminal in DeepSeek TUI. For DeepSeek Harness, connect the OpenMotion MCP tools with the Cordis configuration. DeepSeek Harness setup

The installer uses locally built packages. Windows test packages

Try an online template:

Use OpenMotion to recreate the template at this detail-page URL with my brand kit and copy. Keep the motion and pacing, then open the editable result in Studio for review.

To start from a video instead, supply your reference and use the recreation brief. If your host cannot open Studio beside the conversation, use the returned local project link.

Skills, MCP and CLI

The plugin and MCP server are named openmotion; Tools, Skills and resources use openmotion_*, openmotion-* and openmotion://. Old Tool/resource names remain compatibility aliases; retired Skill entries are removed. Use openmotion-* Skill names and refresh host discovery after upgrading. See naming and installation compatibility.

From the checkout, discover and install the five core workflows with the Skills CLI:

npx skills add ./skills --list
npx skills add ./skills --skill openmotion-director openmotion-production openmotion-template-to-video openmotion-recreate openmotion-video-to-template

This copies instructions; it does not install the runtime or register MCP. Keep the shared documentation available and connect the app separately, or use the integrated local installer above.

Skill Use it for
openmotion-recreate Reconstructing a reference video and comparing the result
openmotion-template-to-video Adapting an existing editable template
openmotion-director Original films, narrative, movement, sound and creative review
openmotion-video-to-template Producing a portable reusable template
openmotion-production Scoped edits, preview, checks, troubleshooting and export

Connect a local agent · Follow the installation guide for your client. Use the configuration below in clients with local stdio MCP support. In a shell-based agent, open the project directory and use the local engine CLI to preview and render the HTML scenes.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openmotion": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/node",
      "args": ["--experimental-strip-types", "/absolute/openmotion/mcp.ts"],
      "env": { "MOTION_DATA_DIR": "/absolute/openmotion-data" }
    }
  }
}

The thirteen public MCP tools cover template discovery and details, project creation and reading, editing, preview, media import and BYOK generation, reusable asset versions, export, version restoration and cancellation. Shared workflow and engine guides are available through MCP resources. Tool contract

Find a template with openmotion_list_templates, inspect it with openmotion_get_template, then create an editable copy with openmotion_create_project. Template catalog

Use npm start for the app and npm run mcp for stdio. Shell-capable agents can inspect and render with the pinned engine CLI returned by the runtime; managed edits retain project revision checks. Native authoring

From a reference to an editable project

Supply the clip and timecodes if your agent cannot open the social link. Start from the reference with the recreation workflow, or use the template workflow when you already have editable source.

Review the template and its Motion.md

Open a template to watch the reference and read its visual style and production notes. Download Motion.md when you want the guide as a reusable file.

Send the template to your agent

Choose Recreate template, copy the instruction and add your brand kit, copy and creative requirements. Your agent installs or connects OpenMotion if needed, then works from the selected template. Open the resulting project in Studio to review the timing, continue editing and export.

System architecture

Editing the timeline in Studio and asking your agent to change a shot both update the same HTML project. The local TypeScript service manages media and revisions. A browser-based rendering engine exports the selected version to MP4.

How the modules work together

Edits made through the project tools include a revision check so an outdated request cannot overwrite newer work. Generated media enters the project when you select it. Each export uses the version saved when the job starts. The exporter checks the file specifications, and you can play the cut to review the picture, sound and timing.

BYOA connects your existing Agent client; the Assets workspace also supports in-app Codex conversations. BYOK connects your supported model accounts. Studio and the local service manage the editable work, while provider credentials remain outside project files. The public phase-one MCP surface contains thirteen tools: nine project tools, two template catalog tools, one BYOK media-use tool and one workspace asset tool. Configure provider keys in Studio, then use openmotion_media_use for model discovery and media generation through the local Gateway service. Use openmotion_assets to upload or generate reusable assets, retain versions and import a chosen version into a film. Asset library guide. Keys remain in the service; the public MCP contract does not include publishing.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A local-first, agent-driven HTML editor designed for generating documents without markdown.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: HTML-Anything is a local-first HTML editor engineered specifically for the AI agent era, operating on the premise that direct HTML generation is superior to Markdown for final human readability. It functions as a workspace that automatically detects and integrates with up to nine popular coding agent CLIs (such as Claude Code, Cursor Agent, and Gemini CLI) found on the user's PATH. The tool leverages existing local API sessions, requiring zero new API keys, to empower AI agents to write, edit, and format rich HTML documents directly. It provides a visual surface mode to preview and manage the agent-generated HTML in real-time.
keyFeatures: Agent CLI Auto-Detection: Automatically discovers and integrates with 9 different coding agent CLIs installed on the system PATH.
Local-First Architecture: Operates entirely locally using existing authenticated CLI sessions without requiring separate API keys.
Direct HTML Editing: Replaces Markdown-based drafting by having agents generate and modify pure HTML for final presentation.
Visual Surface Mode: Provides a live rendering interface to preview and interact with the HTML content generated by the agents.
Zero-Configuration Setup: Works out of the box by reusing the user's existing developer environment and CLI toolchains.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and technical writers who heavily utilize local AI coding agents and prefer generating rich HTML directly over writing Markdown. Ideal for teams requiring efficient AI agents.
